children: Bandhan Bank shares jumped 8% after reports of early-stage stake sale talks involving Abu Dhabi investors and its promoter entity, Bandhan Financial Services.

Shares of Bandhan Bank rose nearly 8 per cent on 13 October 2026 after reports that Abu Dhabi-based investors were in early-stage discussions to acquire a stake in Bandhan Financial Services (BFSL), the promoter entity of the private sector lender. The potential transaction has drawn investor attention to the bank’s ownership structure and the promoter group’s plans to provide an exit to existing investors.

The proposed investment discussions reportedly involve International Holding Company (IHC) and First Abu Dhabi Bank. BFSL, which holds a little over one-third of Bandhan Bank, is working with financial adviser Jefferies to explore strategic investment options.

The promoter entity is reportedly considering the sale of a 25–32 per cent stake to potential strategic investors. The transaction could be valued at up to USD 600 million, although discussions remain at an early stage and no final agreement has been announced. Existing investors, including Singapore’s GIC and the International Finance Corporation (IFC), are among those seeking to monetise their holdings in BFSL.

GIC’s investment arm, Caladium Investment, holds around 16.7 per cent in BFSL, while IFC owns approximately 13.6 per cent, according to reports. The proposed transaction is part of a broader restructuring exercise aimed at providing liquidity to existing shareholders and evaluating options for the promoter group’s investments. The process could also involve potential stake sales in other group businesses.

The potential transaction comes as Bandhan Bank’s promoter group faces a regulatory requirement to reduce its shareholding. Bandhan Financial Holdings, a subsidiary of BFSL, held around 37.5 per cent in the bank at the end of June 2026. The promoter is required to bring its holding down to 26 per cent by 2030 under the bank’s licensing conditions.

A direct stake sale in Bandhan Bank could help the promoter meet this requirement, while an investment at the BFSL level would primarily provide liquidity to existing shareholders of the holding company. The reported discussions have lifted sentiment around the stock, but the eventual impact will depend on the structure, valuation and completion of any transaction. Investors will also watch for formal disclosures from the bank or promoter group as the discussions progress.
